repo.description: The m0saic developer curriculum: minimal example templates, each exercising exactly one knob of the template-authoring surface. Clone it, load it, read it, fork it.

templates.title: 01 · Hello World
templates.description: The smallest correct template, wearing the brand: the pixel-M in a square cell over a greeting, typed props with deterministic defaults, and a validated m0 string. The repo's smoke render.

templates.title: 02 · Hot-Reload Canary
templates.description: Prove your edit loop: the fill comes from a module CONSTANT, so a rebuild + Refresh repos must change it — no app restart, no prop-bag tricks.

templates.title: 03 · Color Tiles
templates.description: Three equal columns, one makeColorTile each — the sources[]-to-tiles mapping, the lavfi color-tile convention, and document.backgroundColor over a wasted base layer.

templates.title: 04 · Aspect-Adaptive Card
templates.description: One template, every aspect: reads ctx.target and flips columns to rows on portrait. Size off ctx.target, never ctx.output — the rule that prevents the classic nested-render bug.

templates.title: 05 · GCD Collapse
templates.description: Two pixel-identical rows from the same weights: literal keeps 100 slots, the default optimized mode collapses to 4. Same look, fraction of the string.

templates.title: 06 · Ratio vs Absolute
templates.description: The same 1:2:1 spelled as a ratio split (recomposes anywhere) and as placeRects (exact pixels, baked to THIS canvas). Identical render, opposite promises.

templates.title: 07 · Overlay Stack
templates.description: 1{3[-,1{1},-]}: base, band on its overlay, badge on the band's overlay. Overlays restore their node's whole rect and paint after it.

templates.title: 08 · Lattice Gutters
templates.description: Base × fiber: a plain gutterless grid as the m0, pixel-exact gutters computed into per-cell placement insets by latticeCellInset. Exact at every canvas, zero DSL cost.

templates.title: 09 · Inset Recovery
templates.description: Exact pixels that survive nesting: placeInsetPieces keeps the string coarse (precision bounded at the lattice basis) while placement.inset recovers every chip byte-exact. The caption prints the precision floor placeRects would bake instead — the cost a parent inherits.

templates.title: 10 · PlaceRect Dock
templates.description: One pixel-exact rect docked bottom-right via placeRect — margins are null tiles, nothing quantizes into your rect. Head-only: the string bakes THIS canvas.

templates.title: 11 · Mask in a Cell
templates.description: A diamond as a masked color tile in a plain ratio cell. Mask bounds scale onto the cell per axis — match their aspect or the shape silently smears.

templates.title: 12 · Quantization: Three Cures
templates.description: The capstone: one 12×3 gridded design through four spellings — naive ratio gutters that wobble N/N+1 px, then inset recovery, snapGrid, and placeRects. Flip the Method enum, watch the lines even out, read the receipts.

templates.title: 13 · Typed Props Tour
templates.description: One prop of each scalar type — string, number, boolean, enum — each visibly driving the render, receipts on the caption. The schema picks the controls; render() is the gate.

templates.title: 14 · Seeded Shuffle
templates.description: Randomness the m0saic way: a REQUIRED seed through mulberry32 — identical props render byte-identical documents, and the caption prints the deal.

templates.title: 15 · Color Props
templates.description: Color props declare themselves: isColor + colorPicker gives the scalar a swatch and the string[] the color-list control. Panel beside palette column.

templates.title: 16 · JSON Data Prop
templates.description: Structured data through one type:"json" prop — collect-ALL validation with remedies, then the records become geometry: one proportional bar per row.

templates.title: 17 · Control Gallery
templates.description: The meta surface, one knob per affordance: placeholder, flavor:"url", bounded+stepped numbers, enum select, ui.label. The real demo is the sidebar.

templates.title: 18 · Error Mosaic
templates.description: Failing on-canvas, usefully: collect EVERY problem with a remedy and return makeErrorMosaic — a renderable report card instead of a dead preview.

templates.title: 19 · Image Card
templates.description: One image through the whole media pipeline: raw path prop, ctx.media probe, slugified asset key, {kind:"file"} entry, media source — and the contain-vs-cover decision on a knob.

templates.title: 20 · Folder Contact Strip
templates.description: type:"media[]" + the folder picker: an array of probed paths mapped to per-file assets and sources; the strip resplits to the count.

templates.title: 21 · Probe Card
templates.description: ctx.media is the host's ffprobe registry, keyed by the RAW prop string. Pick any file and the card prints its entry — the facts every layout decision is built on.

templates.title: 22 · Time-Range Clip
templates.description: The time-range picker pair (clipStartMs/clipEndMs + videoFromProp) renders ONE two-handle scrubber — and the window lands as playback.clipStartMs + clipDurationMs (start + LENGTH).

templates.title: 23 · Time-Ranges Medley
templates.description: The MULTI-range control: one json prop (Array<{startMs,endMs,label?}>) with picker:"time-ranges" — the studio writes the whole array through it, and every window renders as its own medley column off the same assetId.

templates.title: 24 · Luma Badge
templates.description: ctx.analysis.regionLuminance picks the badge's contrast from the pixels under it — and the OPTIONAL-analysis law: degrade to a STATED default, never a silent one.

templates.title: 25 · Play Speed
templates.description: playback.playSpeed: source time vs output time, with the caption doing the arithmetic — a 2s source at 4x lasts 500ms of output and loop fills the rest.

templates.title: 26 · Audio Mix
templates.description: Audio sources contribute no pixels — per-source audio.volume sets the blend, and the mute idiom (audio.enabled=false, source KEPT) keeps the document's shape stable.

templates.title: 27 · URL Asset
templates.description: The {kind:"url"} manifest entry: host-fetched remote media with the costs stated on canvas — offline fails, bytes drift, no probe before fetch. Prefer files for reproducibility.

templates.title: 28 · Text, Three Ways
templates.description: The same word through all three text pipelines, side by side: drawtext (ffmpeg, expr-capable, host fonts), the svg rasterizer (bundled font baked to geometry), and mask-carved glyphs (text as a mask any source can wear).

templates.title: 29 · Fit Text
templates.description: Nothing soft-wraps — fitting is the template's job. One box, three strategies (wrap the block, force one line, skip fitting and clip), and a caption printing the measured width against the box.

templates.title: 30 · Count Up
templates.description: A drawtext counter ramping 0 → value over the clip: content.kind "expr" + eval "frame" + renderMode "video", the three fields that must agree. Flip Freeze as a still to see the quiet failure.

templates.title: 31 · Carved Type
templates.description: The word becomes an inline-mask and the picture plays through it: textToPath makes glyphs into a path, the path clips an ordinary media source, and the source underneath can be anything.

templates.title: 32 · Shape Masks
templates.description: There are no shape primitives — every shape is a color tile wearing an SVG path. Circle, ellipse, rounded rect and pill, each authored against the cell's own box, with the caption printing the path math.

templates.title: 33 · Path Mask
templates.description: A donut, and the two rules behind it: a shape inside another cuts a hole only when it is DRAWN the other way round (the two directions cancel; draw them the same way and the middle fills in silently), and `matte` renders the area outside the path at a chosen alpha instead of clipping it away.

templates.title: 34 · Child Mosaic
templates.description: A complete document rendered inside one tile: children + a {type:"mosaic", ref} source, evaluated bottom-up. The child's grid grows while the parent's m0 stays two cells — and a procedural child keeps its aspect only if it declares its own size.

templates.title: 35 · Rotate Headroom
templates.description: effects.rotate spins content inside a buffer that never grows, so corners clip. The cure isn't a bigger inset — it's a child whose declared size is the rotated bounding box, carrying the rotation instead.

templates.title: 36 · Nested Template
templates.description: renderNestedTemplate calls another registered template and returns a document to drop into children. The slot option is the lesson: hand the child its real pixel box and it lays itself out for that box instead of for your canvas.

templates.title: 37 · Nested Badge (internal)
templates.description: The child half of compose/nested-template: a badge that sizes everything off ctx.target, so it fills whatever slot the caller gives it. Marked internal — not a top-level pick, but it renders standalone, which is how you debug a child.

templates.title: 38 · Camera Follow
templates.description: A keyframed camera walk described as rects and times: followCamera turns targets into per-frame focus expressions over a child mosaic's own coordinate space, with an optional pull-back — and viewport rects showing exactly what each settle will frame.

templates.title: 39 · Theme Provider
templates.description: The PRODUCER half of theming: publishTheme(tokens, { alias }) emits a data source carrying a token set, and every downstream template reading that alias picks it up. One mode prop re-skins the whole chain.

templates.title: 40 · Theme Tokens
templates.description: The CONSUMER half of theming, and the three places tokens come from: local constants, a pipeline producer on ctx.upstreamData, or a provider called by id right here. applyTheme overlays whatever arrived, per key.

templates.title: 41 · Reduce to One
templates.description: The same grid spelled two ways: inline (the parent's m0 grows with the density) or pushed into a child (the parent stays one cell). Identical pixels, with both string lengths printed so the refactor is a number.

templates.title: 42 · Two Scenes
templates.description: The smallest pipeline: two documents concatenated into one file. A step IS a document (own m0, own canvas, own exact durationMs), and a d-ms transition OVERLAPS them — the output is A + B − d.

templates.title: 43 · Fan Out
templates.description: emit:"multi" writes one file per output step, each at its own canvas — the only way one template delivers several geometries. The variants re-LAY OUT rather than scaling.

templates.title: 44 · PNG Sequence
templates.description: A frame sequence is emit:"multi" where every step is an image. Files land as {base}-{step.name}.png, so zero-padded names are the template's job — the engine only guarantees the name it was given.

templates.title: 45 · Encode Matrix
templates.description: One render, many deliverables, no pipeline: `encodes` declares post-render transcode passes off a single master. Codec, container, even size (as a stretching scale pass) — never fps, duration or layout.

templates.title: 46 · Ref Mirror
templates.description: A ref source mirrors another cell's rendered pixels by flattenedStableKey: the target renders once and every mirror decorates its own copy. N mirrors, one decode.

templates.title: 47 · Ref Across Steps
templates.description: A ref with stepIndex is a BACK-EDGE: a later step shows an earlier step's exact pixels, no re-render. Back-edges only, plus the handoff idiom where the producer self-stamps its own coordinates.

templates.title: 48 · Ref Reframe
templates.description: A mirror whose slot differs in shape and length: placement.fit reframes the pixels, playback.loopMode fills the tail. Nothing is re-rendered — one intermediate, per-consumer decoration.

templates.title: 49 · Nested Pipeline
templates.description: A children entry may be a PIPELINE: it renders first and the parent consumes its stitched output as one tile. The slot's duration and canvas win, emit:"multi" downgrades, and loopMode fills any shortfall.

templates.title: 50 · Fixture Fetcher
templates.description: Where data enters: a type:"data" source publishes a payload downstream templates read as ctx.upstreamData[alias]. tier:"capability" is what makes ctx.secrets exist, and only a derived marker is published — never the value.

templates.title: 51 · Pure Adapter
templates.description: A pure function between channels: read one block, publish another. Reshaping needs no capability tier and no network, so it stays core tier — and a missing upstream degrades to an empty result rather than throwing.

templates.title: 52 · Data Card
templates.description: The consumer end: read ctx.upstreamData[alias] and draw it. The three links agree on an alias and a shape, never on each other's ids, and the card names what it read so a broken chain shows in the picture.

templates.title: 53 · Sidecar JSON
templates.description: doc.sidecars writes files beside the render — each key becomes {output-basename}.{key}.json. Declared on the template, attached to the document: a file for what comes after m0saic, where a data source is a channel for the next template.

templates.title: 54 · Sidecar Text
templates.description: { kind: "text", ext, content } writes the string verbatim, which is how real formats ship. Captions prove the point: burned-in subtitles are pixels, a .vtt beside the video is a track a player can style.

templates.title: 55 · Render Lite
templates.description: The preview stand-in. Declares renderLite so the editor draws a cheap card while you poke props, and the real N-by-N grid renders only on Make — the one optional surface that falls back to render when absent instead of simply not happening.

templates.title: 56 · Render Cover
templates.description: A friendly first frame for a template that fails fast. render() still reports exactly what is missing when it has no clip; renderCover puts a welcome page there on a pure-default open — opt-in, dismissed by the first prop edit, and silently skipped (never synthesized) when absent or broken.

templates.title: 57 · Render Tutorial
templates.description: The only lesson here that builds its own tutorial instead of using the curriculum's standard page — because building one is what it teaches. Three pages as a pipeline, each declaring its own durationMs, proving that a tutorial owns its timing and never reads ctx.target.durationMs.

packs.title: Basics
packs.description: Hello world, the hot-reload loop, color tiles, and sizing off ctx.target — the smallest possible templates that still do everything right.

packs.title: Geometry
packs.description: The m0 geometry contract as runnable lessons: quantization you can predict, GCD collapse, ratio vs absolute, passthrough donation, overlays, lattice gutters (both spellings), inset recovery, placeRect, and masks as fiber.

packs.title: Props
packs.description: The typed props surface as runnable lessons: one knob of every scalar type, seeded determinism, self-declaring color controls, structured json data, the meta/control affordances, and failing usefully with makeErrorMosaic.

packs.title: Media
packs.description: Files, folders, probes, and time: the media prop pipeline, ctx.media as the host's ffprobe registry, the time-range scrubber pair, content-aware analysis with stated fallbacks, playSpeed, the audio mix + mute idiom, and the url-asset trade-off.

packs.title: Text
packs.description: Text that renders right: the three glyph pipelines side by side (drawtext, svg rasterizer, mask-carved), then the per-technique deep dives — fitting, expressions, and carved type.

packs.title: Masks
packs.description: Shapes without shape primitives: the everyday paths (circle, ellipse, rounded rect, pill) authored against their cell, then the hand-written path where winding cuts holes and `matte` turns the leftover box into a translucent wash.

packs.title: Compose
packs.description: Documents inside documents: children and bottom-up evaluation, real geometry as headroom for rotation, calling another template with a slot, a keyframed camera over a space you own, a theme taken from upstream, and the reduce-to-one refactor all of it enables.

packs.title: Pipelines
packs.description: More than one document, and more than one file: steps and transitions, emit single vs multi, encodes as a separate axis, ref sources mirroring rendered pixels within a doc and back across steps, and a pipeline living inside a tile.

packs.title: Data
packs.description: Facts flowing through a render: publishing a payload on the upstream channel (and what the capability tier buys you), reshaping it with a pure adapter, drawing it, and writing files beside the deliverable — JSON for machines, verbatim text for real formats like captions.

packs.title: Surfaces
packs.description: The entry points past `render`, all editor-only and all opt-in: a cheap preview stand-in that falls back to render, a welcome cover that lets render stay strict, and a bespoke tutorial that owns its own timing.
